name: Auth0
description: Auth0 is an identity platform whose Management API exposes tenant Applications, Connections, users, organizations, and configuration to tenant-authorized administrative clients.
agentUseSummary: Auth0 cannot be newly connected under Relay's provider-owned OAuth model. Auth0 explicitly blocks third-party applications, including AI agents and external partners, from its Management API; Relay therefore mounts no credentials or tools and does not substitute a customer-owned administrative M2M secret without a separately authorized product decision.

blocked.description: Customer-owned tenant M2M client IDs and secrets are a distinct high-risk administrative credential product that is not authorized in V1.

providerSetup.blocker: Auth0's enhanced third-party application controls explicitly do not support Auth0 system APIs, including the Management API, for externally operated partners or AI agents. The supported tenant-owned M2M flow requires each customer to create and authorize an administrative application and share its client secret, which is a materially different product not authorized by this convergence batch.
providerSetup.nextAction: Keep Auth0 unavailable unless a separate product decision explicitly authorizes customer-owned exact-tenant M2M credentials with narrow read:clients/read:connections grants, or Auth0 publishes a supported third-party Management API authorization contract.

evidence.supports: Auth0 explicitly lists Management API, MFA API, My Account API, and My Orgs API as unsupported system APIs for third-party applications and says they cannot be granted system-API access.
Auth0 defines external partners and AI agents as third-party operators and states Auth0 system APIs are not accessible in third-party user flows.
Auth0 Support documents the April 2026 restriction and the unauthorized-client failure for third-party requests targeting Auth0 system API audiences.
Auth0 documents production Management API access through a tenant-created and authorized Machine-to-Machine Application using its client credentials.
Auth0 documents that Management API requests require an appropriately scoped Management API access token rather than an end-user login or ID token.
